Topic: The Central Limit Theorem (CLT): From Chaos to Order

Target audience: University students (Introductory Statistics)

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite: The Concept of Distributions

Lecture lines:
Distributions track frequency of occurrence.
Normal distributions show bell curves.
Other distributions appear skewed or uniform.

Planned animations:
Draw a generic distribution curve #FFFFFF on screen.
Highlight the peak of the curve in #FFD700.
Label the peak 'Mean' using #FFD700 text.
Show data points spreading below the curve.
Fade out the curve leaving the mean.

Section: section_2 — The Problem: Does the Parent Distribution Matter?

Lecture lines:
Does the parent distribution shape matter?
Let's sample from non-normal populations.
Do sample means follow original patterns?

Planned animations:
Show two different shapes: Square and Triangle.
Transform both shapes into a cloud of dots.
Show histograms of these dots below each.
Animate dots forming a Bell Curve.
Overlay the Bell Curves on both histograms.

Section: section_3 — The Experiment: Building the Sampling Distribution

Lecture lines:
Take many samples of size n.
Calculate the mean for each sample.
Plot means as size n increases.
Observe the shape transforming into curves.
Bell shapes emerge from chaotic data.

Planned animations:
Start with a population set in #FFFFFF.
Randomly select 5 samples in #FF4500.
Calculate the mean of these samples.
Plot this mean as a dot on a new graph.
Repeat the process to build a sampling distribution.

Section: section_4 — The Core Revelation: The Central Limit Theorem

Lecture lines:
The Central Limit Theorem defines this.
Sample means approach a Normal Distribution.
Valid for any original population shape.
Required sample size typically n equals 30.
Chaos transforms into stable bell curves.

Planned animations:
Display the sample size n = 5, 10, 30.
Show the distribution narrowing as n increases.
Display CLT MathTex formula in #FFFFFF.
Highlight the normal distribution shape in #32CD32.
Blink the formula to emphasize it.

Section: section_5 — Why It Matters: Real-World Application

Lecture lines:
CLT is the foundation of inference.
We predict populations from small samples.
Accurate estimates require minimal data points.

Planned animations:
Display a real-world scenario (e.g., polling data).
Show the margin of error narrowing.
Use a checkmark symbol (scale 1.0) in #32CD32.
Show confidence intervals converging.
Final summary text appearing in #FFFFFF.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Distributions track frequency of occurrence.",
            "Normal distributions show bell curves.",
            "Other distributions appear skewed or uniform."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Concept of Distributions", lecture_lines)
        
        # Prepare objects
        curve = FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.exp(-x**2), x_range=[-3, 3], color=WHITE)
        peak = Dot(curve.point_from_proportion(0.5), color=WHITE)
        mean_label = Text("Mean", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        points = VGroup(*[Dot(curve.point_from_proportion(i/10), radius=0.05) for i in range(11)])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(Create(curve), run_time=1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            peak.animate.set_color(GOLD),
            mean_label.animate.set_color(GOLD)
        )
        self.place_at_grid(mean_label, 'B4')
        self.add(mean_label)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED)
        self.play(FadeIn(points), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(curve), FadeOut(peak), FadeOut(mean_label), FadeOut(points))

        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["CLT is the foundation of inference.", "We predict populations from small samples.", "Accurate estimates require minimal data points."]
        self.setup_layout("Why It Matters: Real-World Application", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a real-world scenario (smartphone battery example)
        phone = SVGMobject("smartphone") if False else RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.2, height=2, width=1.2, fill_opacity=0.5, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(phone, "C2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(phone))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show confidence intervals / Margin of Error
        interval = VGroup(
            Line(LEFT*1.5, RIGHT*1.5, color=WHITE),
            Dot(color=RED),
            Line(UP*0.2, DOWN*0.2, color=WHITE).shift(LEFT*1.0),
            Line(UP*0.2, DOWN*0.2, color=WHITE).shift(RIGHT*1.0)
        )
        self.place_at_grid(interval, "E4", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(interval))
        self.play(interval.animate.scale(0.6)) # Narrowing
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#87CEEB")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Checkmark
        checkmark = Tex(r"$\checkmark$", color="#32CD32")
        self.place_at_grid(checkmark, "B4", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(GrowFromCenter(checkmark))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#32CD32")
        self.wait(2)
